description: Solo participant interested in data provenance, reproducible analysis, and clear visual explanations. Exploring MODIS and VIIRS hotspot records to support comparisons of historical and recent burning activity. This is a one-person team and is not recruiting.
summary: Burning Atlas connects Aqua MODIS history with S-NPP VIIRS hotspot records in an interactive 2003–2024 calendar for Northeast Asia. A frozen seasonal count model estimates Aqua-reference detections while preserving original observations. Users select an area and period, inspect uncertain changes, and download counts, hotspot records and validation evidence. The prototype improves count agreement but retains summer and local biases; full long-term harmonization remains unverified.
details:
The web application shows monthly and annual hotspot patterns within [120,130)°E and [40,50)°N. Users choose the whole footprint, quadrants or individual 1° cells and a date range. Four views distinguish connected counts, original Aqua observations, original VIIRS observations and adjusted VIIRS expectations. A selected month exposes its historical-median comparison, connected year change, weather context and limitations. Downloads include monthly CSV, calendar SVG, original selected-month hotspot records, full-precision model coefficients and evaluation tables.

We define the quantity as selected daytime hotspot detection records per 1° cell and UTC month, not unique fire events. Aqua confidence is at least 30; VIIRS confidence is nominal or high. We remove exact duplicates and apply no FRP cutoff. A seasonal negative-binomial model learns the relationship between VIIRS counts and Aqua counts during 2013–2018, including monthly count responses, location and NASA POWER weather. All coefficients and standardization remain fixed for later estimates. The illustrative connected history retains Aqua counts through 2018 and uses VIIRS-derived Aqua-reference expected counts for 2019–2024. The switch year is a test, not Aqua retirement. Eight known archive-issue months remain unavailable. Selecting an area or date never refits the model or forces a match to an observed test-month total.

The seasonal negative-binomial model was selected using a declared equal-average-rank rule for count WAPE, historical-median direction and connected year-change direction in forward 2015–2018 predictions. In 2019–2024 developmental assessment, the daily_pass_grid alternative has lower June–July bias (-6.24%) and fewer median/year-change direction errors (5/64 and 11/61), but higher count WAPE (16.76% versus 12.95%). We retain the earlier selection rather than choose retrospectively on these later results. These later periods were already examined during development and are not untouched independent validation.

On 64 full-area evaluation months from 2019–2024, selected-model count WAPE is 12.95%, compared with 20.09% for a monthly-ratio baseline. June–July aggregate bias remains −28.67%. Point-estimate historical-median errors are 7/64 and connected year-change direction errors are 14/61. Empirical ranges leave unsupported comparisons unresolved, with no guaranteed coverage. These periods were inspected during development and are not untouched independent validation. Across 100 individual 1-degree cells, median count WAPE is 45.61%, and 44 cells exceed 50%; quadrant WAPE ranges from 14.54% to 20.21%. Full valid observing opportunity and the long-term stability of the Aqua reference remain unverified. The app does not provide live warnings, fire forecasts, ignition causes, global calibration or 2025–2026 data. It implements an empirical harmonization prototype, not a finally validated common fire history.

All hotspot types are retained. In an earlier candidate's selected failure-month audit, over half of Aqua detections in several summer months carry inferred type 2 (other static land source). These labels do not identify confirmed factories or establish the cause of summer bias. NASA reports a historical VIIRS type-label bug; our CSV Collection label alone does not establish the upstream correction revision.

Relative to the 2013–2018 same-cell, same-calendar-month detection-time reference, the median Aqua shift is about +12 minutes in 2023 and +30 minutes in 2024. These are detected-record local solar times, not measurements of every overpass. Aqua source labels also change from 6.03 to 61.03. Reference-system drift and processing differences have not been separated from model error.

2022 excludes April, July and August; 2024 excludes May, June, July, September and November. Partial-year sums are not annual totals. The 2022 connected sum of 4,183.88 and Aqua sum of 4,728 cover the same nine usable months; the returned Aqua archive sum of 7,943 includes all twelve months and is not a like-for-like comparator.

ChatGPT/Codex assisted literature organization, code, analysis and interface/document creation under Hyeze’s direction. Model outputs were compared with observed records and limitations are disclosed. NASA has not independently reviewed or endorsed the prototype.
